findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Inspector observed missing Employee Health Reporting Agreements for two of the three staff members who were present during today’s inspection. All staff who work in a food establishment must be informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report food-borne illness symptoms and diagnoses to their employees. Inspector will verify compliance on 6/1/26. Ensure all staff read and sign Employee Health Reporting Agreements within 30 days of hire, to be maintained on file for inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: The inspector observed the basin of the back of house hand washing sink to contain a bucket and cleaning supplies. CORRECTED- the inspector moved the items to wash hands. Education occurred with the Person in Charge (PIC) regarding hand sink availability. All designated hand washing sinks must be used for hand washing only.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 3 cans of food dented along the seams. CORRECTED- items were removed from service. Ensure all hermetically sealed containers are inspected for bulging, rust, and dents along the seams to prevent the entry and harborage of Botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A large quantity of foods that are either temperature control for food safety (TCS) or labeled “keep refrigerated” were observed to have an internal temperature between 46-60F in the open air cooler. Foods include but are not limited to: calzones, deli sandwiches, desserts with cream cheese icing, sandwiches, cottage cheese, hard boiled (and peeled) eggs, cheesewiches, Naked juice, and pickles (labeled “keep refrigerated”). In addition, a pallet of Simply Juices labeled “Keep refrigerated” was stored at room temperature in dry storage. CORRECTED- items in the open air cooler were removed from service, and the PIC ensured the inspector that all foods and drinks aforementioned would be discarded after logging waste. All TCS foods (including those labeled “keep refrigerated”- the label is the law) under cold holding must be at or under 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens that cause food-borne illnesses.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The mocha iced coffee bag was observed without date marking. CORRECTED- the inspector asked the PIC when the coffee bag was opened. PIC stated the bag was opened two days ago, and marked the bag with the corresponding date. Once TCS foods that are ready to eat and require cold holding are opened, they must bear date mark to be used or discarded within 7 days time.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the open air cooler to be failing to hold TCS foods at an internal temperature of 41F or below (see violation #22). Inspector recommends having the machine serviced to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. All cold holding units must have the capacity to maintain safe food temperatures. Inspector will return on 6/1/26 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two stem thermometers 5-8F out of calibration. CORRECTED- the inspector modeled calibration using the ice water method to the PIC. Ensure all thermometers are maintained to be calibrated according to the manufacturer's instructions to provide accurate internal temperatures for TCS foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets of multiple standing coolers to be in disrepair. The following coolers need their gaskets repaired or replaced. Those housing: water, Gatorade, Celsius, Alani/ Bang, Monster (both) , and Mountain Dew. Ensure these repairs take place by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed build up on multiple nonfood contact surfaces:
1) A significant accumulation of ice in the blue bunny sliding freezer. Defrost and remove build up.
2) Soil debris on the outside of the ice shoots (soda stations).
Nonfood contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, and prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wet mop stored in the basin of the mop bucket. CORRECTED- education was conducted and the mop was positioned to air dry. Mops function to clean up fats, oils, and greases- therefore must be placed in a position to air dry immediately after use to prevent the harborage of bacteria.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The person in charge (PIC) had an expired Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) Certificate. Ensure CFPM is renewed and maintained every 5 years. A CFPM should be present during all times during which food is being handled or prepared.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The inspector observed the hand washing sink to contain a scoop and lid. CORRECTED- the inspector moved the items to wash hands. Education occurred with the Person in Charge (PIC) regarding hand sink availability. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for hand washing only, to incentivize hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: The iced coffee bags were observed without date marking. CORRECTED- the inspector asked the PIC when the coffee bags were opened. PIC stated they were opened when the new shipment came in on 09/22, and marked the bags with the corresponding date. Once temperature control for food safety (TCS) cold held items are opened, they must bear date mark to be used or discarded within 7 days time.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ice machine cleaner to be stored over soda boxes in the back storage room. CORRECTED- the cleaner was moved away from the food products. Ensure chemicals are always stored below or away from food products to prevent a contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The PIC verified that the facility does not have ambient thermometers. Ambient thermometers (when properly positioned) display the temperature of the warmest part of the cold holding unit, which help the facility identify when the cold holding units are not properly working. Obtain ambient thermometers for cold holding units housing TCS foods (milk, cheese, eggs, meats) by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple single service boxes to be stored on the ground; including cups, straws, and trays. CORRECTED- PIC moved single service boxes onto other boxes that were neither foods or food contact surfaces. Ensure single service articles are stored at least 6 inches above the ground to prevent potential contamination of food contact surfaces at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the gaskets of multiple standing coolers to be in disrepair. The following coolers need their gaskets repaired or replaced. Those housing: water, Gatorade, Celsius, Ghost, Monster, and Mountain Dew. Ensure these repairs take place by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Facility is currently using Purell sanitizing wipes to clean food contact surfaces. To continue using Purell to sanitize food contact surfaces, the facility must obtain Purell test strips to verify that the solution is holding the proper sanitizing concentration. Either buy quaternary ammonia to sanitize food contact surfaces  (which the facility has test strips for), OR obtain and use Purell test strips.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed an accumulation of milk residue on the floor beneath the milk in the retail cooler. Increase the frequency at which this area is being cleaned to prevent the contamination of food contact and nonfood contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
PIC could not locate the facility’s employee reporting agreement. Inspector provided a blank reporting agreement to be copied, reviewed, and signed by employees. If this information is already covered in employee trainings or handbook, keep the information accessible within the facility for review during health inspections.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No paper towels were available at the handwashing sink near the 3 compartment sink. CORRECTED- Employee provided paper towels upon request. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon inspector’s arrival, the handsink near the 3 compartment sink was observed with soda fountain nozzles in the basin. CORRECTED- PIC removed the items from the handsink. Ensure handsinks are maintained clear and accessible to promote frequent handwashing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Original cheese and jalapeno cheese were observed in dispensers without date markings indicating when they were opened. CORRECTED- Open cheese bags were voluntarily discarded. Replacement bags were labeled with the date they were opened and will be used or discarded according to manufacturer instruction (not exceeding 7 days).
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Chili in the dispenser was observed with a date marking of 11/14. CORRECTED- Chili was voluntarily discarded. Ensure chili is used or discarded according to manufacturer’s instructions, not exceeding 7 days.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Quat sanitizer solution was not available in the food service area. CORRECTED- Solution at 400ppm was provided during inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Facility does not have quat test strips available. Ensure test strips are available for any sanitizer used in the facility.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Shelves in the walk-in cooler were observed with an accumulation of dust and mold. Clean shelves as often as necessary to prevent accumulation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.  [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Milk residue was observed on the floor under the milk shelves. Clean the walk-in floor as often as necessary to maintain it clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Trim is missing from the wall between the mop sink and the back door so that the end of the wall covering is exposed. Replace trim so that wall is smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Food handler training could not be verified for employees. PIC stated that employees complete internal food handler training. The employee “scorecards” did not show food handler certificates. Provide proof that employees have completed food handler training that meets the requirements of the Illinois Food Code.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No paper towels were available at the handwashing sink near the 3 compartment sink. CORRECTED- Employee provided paper towels upon request. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No soap was available at the handwashing sink near the roller grills. Ensure soap is always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
No date markings were present on the open creamer packages in the dispensers. PIC indicated that they typically go through multiple bags of each creamer in a week. CORRECTED- Creamers will be used or discarded by the end of operation today. Ensure products in dispensers are labeled with appropriate date markings.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (D) Approved date marking systems. (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container. (F) Does not apply to shellstock.  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Jalapeno cheese in the dispenser was observed with a date marking of 10/24. Dispenser indicates that cheese sauce is good for 5 days. This package should have been discarded on 10/29. CORRECTED- Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Quat sanitizer solution was not available in the food service area. CORRECTED- Solution at 200ppm was provided during inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11 Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Drain plugs for the 3 compartment sink are not adequate in preventing water from draining out of the sink basins. Provide effective drain stoppers so that sink basins may be filled and used to wash, rinse, and sanitize equipment and utensils. See General Comments for additional information.
4-301.12: (A) Sink with 3-compartments shall be provided for EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS. (B) Sinks shall be capable of accommodating the immersion of the largest piece of EQUIPMENT or UTENSIL. A machine or alternative option can be used. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Trim is missing from the wall between the mop sink and the back door so that the end of the wall covering is exposed. Replace trim so that wall is smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Dirty water observed in a mop bucket near the entrance to the food prep area/back room. Discard mop water promptly after use to limit pest harborage conditions.
6-501.114: The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Food handler training could not be verified for employees. PIC stated that employees complete internal food handler training. The employee “scorecards” did not show food handler certificates, and, most of the employees had not completed one of the several food safety modules. Provide proof that employees have completed food handler training that meets the requirements of the Illinois Food Code.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed during inspection for handwashing; cleaning of food contact surfaces, and hot holding. Also, none of the full time staff on duty at the time of inspection had a food manager certification. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at follow-up inspection on 10/24/22.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 None of the full time staff working at the time of inspection had a food manager certification. Another person from corporate was on-site that had a CFM but was not in charge of food service and/or overseeing food service at the time of inspection. Requirement of a FDA food code were discussed. See general comments for additional information.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee did not was hands prior to attempting adjustment of the nozzle at the small cheese sauce dispenser. Employee was observed touching the food contact surface of the cheese sauce bag that inserts into the dispensing apparatus. Handwashing prior to working with food and food dispensing equipment was discussed. Employee washed hands prior to continuing with task and cheese sauce in question was discarded due to what appeared to be a faulty insert.  
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Spatula was observed in the basin of the handwashing sink in the dish washing area. Spatula was removed from the handwashing sink by inspector to allow access for handwashing. Employee preparing sani-bucket was later observed using the handwashing sink as a temporary staging area by placing the bucket in the basin while adding tablets to solution. Proper use of handwashing sink was discussed with staff. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Stem of food thermometers and one of the holding cases were soiled with buildup of food debris. Thermometers and cases were removed for cleaning. Ensure proper cleaning and sanitizing of thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or quat solution are used to wipe stem during prep/temperature checks, ensure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) (A)(1) 1. Dispensed portions of cheese and chili sauces from condiment dispenser were observed with internal temperatures of 109F and 104F. Product was placed in the dispenser the day prior based on information provided. Sauces were discarded.
2. Breakfast tornadoes on roller grills were not rotating. Surface temperatures were below 135F, and internal temperature was observed at 126F. Products were removed for discard as staff were preparing to transition to lunch service. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Gehl’s dispenser used for chili and cheese sauces was holding around 100F and unable to maintain product at 135F. Per information provided, sauces were placed in the dispenser the day prior. Gehl’s dispenser was removed from food service area, and shift manager called company during inspection. Gehl’s will replace the dispenser in ~1 week. 
Equipment for cooling and heating food, and holding cold and hot food, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Quat sanitizer solution was not available in the food service area. Solution at 200ppm was provided during inspection. See general comments for additional information. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Cartons of raw shell eggs were stored above bottled water in the cooler. Store manager rearranged product to allow for proper storage of raw eggs on the bottom shelf. 
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed on surfaces inside the microwave. Ensure cleaning of the microwave occurs at least up to every 24hrs or more frequently depending on use.
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Open packages of smoked sausages, maple sausage links, and breakfast Tornados were without date marks in the walk-in cooler. Store manager was unsure as to when the sausages were first opened, but the Tornados were just opened this morning. Sausages were wasted and discarded during inspection. Tornados were kept for breakfast service. If Tornados were not served by the end of breakfast a date mark would be placed on the package.
-Creamers in dispenser were also without date marks. Store Manager noted they were just placed in the dispenser today and have a hold time of 3 days. Date marks are to be placed on the storage compartments where product is located when placed in the dispenser. Manager dated the creamers. **Ensure proper date marking of ready to eat, TCS foods.**
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Quat solution in sani-bucket available for use in food service area was observed at a concentration above 400ppm with inspector’s instant change test strips and facility’s litmus paper strips. Color change for test strips was off the chart. Fresh solution was prepared at 200ppm. Ensure test strips are used to verify sanitizer concentration of 200-400ppm as directed on label instructions. 
Chemical sanitizers must meet the concentration and use requirements specified by 40 CFR 180.940. Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was checked with ice point method to verify accuracy and observed reading below 30F (~28F). Thermometer were calibrated to 32°F. Food thermometer maintenance was discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Popcorn scoop was stored in a box with miscellaneous items in the cabinet below the popcorn machine. Scoop was taken to 3 part sink to be cleaned and sanitized prior to next use. Properly store the scoop between uses so it is protected from potential contamination.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in a protected location when used with non-TCS foods.

Equipment shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

A) counters under roller grills (dust/debris);  and
B) microwave shelf (dust).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

Staff were advised the mixing wand needs to be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs. Mixing wand was to be cleaned and sanitized prior to next customer use. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours. 

Outer surfaces of ice shoots at the soda machines were soiled with mold buildup along the sides. Clean and sanitize the ice shoots.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11 Plastic containers used for food storage were observed stacked on the 3 part sink drain board with moisture on inner surfaces. It appeared containers went through ware washing and were then stacked. Ensure proper air drying of cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils.
After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining as specified in the first paragraph of 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), before contact with food, and may not be cloth dried.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Manager filled a cup with water to calibrate the food thermometer at the food counter handsink. Manager was advised on proper use of handsinks for handwashing only and that signage should be placed at the sink in an attempt to deter using the sink for other purposes. After discussing this the ice water solution was also dumped at the front handsink. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using the food counter handsink for purposes other than handwashing. Staff should do their best to advise customers on this also.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-bucket at food service area was at 0ppm quat. Solution was remade and observed at 200ppm. Manager was advised on use of warm water, as directed on instructions for use, to ensure tablets dissolve properly.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Follow label directions, and use test strips to verify concentration of solutions.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Hotdogs on one roller grill were observed with surface temperatures at 106F-107F. The internal temperature of one hotdog was observed at 108F. Employee noted the hotdogs in question were put on around 6-6:30am and should have already been to temperature. All products were discarded. Ensure the roller grill is turned up hot enough to thoroughly reheat the precooked, ready to eat roller grill items to proper temperature as specified on the product directions. Items should reach at least 135F prior to service. 
Ready to eat, TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in an inspected/regulated food processing plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Several small flies were observed in the cabinet beneath the iced coffee and cold brew machines where a drain was located. Buildup of splash and debris were noted in the cabinet, which was likely contributing to the presence of pests. Store manager cleaned the area in question during inspection. Manager was advised on use of fly strips in the cabinet to help further eliminate flies. 
NOTE: Fly strips may be used as long as they are placed in appropriate areas that do not pose a potential risk of cross contamination to food, clean equipment, or single service articles. 
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

The 3 part sink may need to be replaced if the divider cannot be permanently and properly repaired to eliminate water leakage between the compartments. Manager stated she would put in a work order. In the meantime, manager was advised to have staff do ware washing from right to left since the third compartment can maintain a proper sanitize solution to allow for manual submersion of 30-60 seconds as required for proper contact time prior to air drying.

Equipment shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).

Employees shall properly wash their hands at designated handsinks whenever hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:

Manager spoke with maintenance via phone during the inspection. The area in question needs to be welded. A work order will be placed. Also, only one stopper was available for use in the sinks. Once the wash step was completed the employee doing dishes had to switch the stopper to the third compartment to allow for sanitizer solution to be prepared. Manager will purchase an additional stopper to allow for detergent solution and sanitizing solution to be setup properly at the same time during ware washing.

For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used.

Employee washing dishes and manager were advised on proper ware washing and sanitizing with bleach solution (200ppm concentration; submerge items for 60 seconds before air drying). Items getting cleaned at the time of inspection were properly sanitized.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250 A number of the sandwiches on the top tier of the open air cooler were observed warm (48-51F). A sandwich was probed and found to be 48F. That sandwich was discarded. the remaining sandwiches were just stocked after lunch and were allowed to be moved to the walk-in cooler. A stem thermometer was placed on the top tier so that proper temperature monitoring could take place. The facility monitors this cooler every two hours. The cooler is located directly infront of the front doors.   All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g The facility has chlorine test strips but no strips are available for the quat sanitizer that is in use. Provide quat test strips. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed an old sani-bucket with 0ppm residual chemical. The water is observed cold and frothy. Discussed changing the bucket at least every four hours or as needed to maintain 200ppm Quat. Water was emptied during the inspection. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the last four racks of the walk-in cooler to be soiled with molds. Clean the racks. The remaining racks are observed in clean condition. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed the coffee filters to be stored uncovered on the top of the coffee machine. Move the filters so the surface is protected from overhead and store contamination. Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 750-1120(b) Observed two measuring cups and a drain catch in the backroom handsink. Items were pulled from the handsink basin during the inspection. Cease allowing items to obstruct use of the sink. Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floors throughout are observed clean. The floor in the backroom by the three compartment sink and handsink is observed soiled with water and dirt debris. Clean the floor.  Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280 Observed coats being stored on the soda syrup box rack and on the rack holding foods by the walk-in cooler. Coats were moved during the inspection. Discussed placing hooks on the wall by the walk-in cooler for coats.  Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment: 750-1380b The soiled linen basket is observed holding a medium sized pile of soiled cloths that have begun to become a breeding ground for pests. Make sure that linens are laundered frequently enough to prevent pests from breeding. Soiled clothes and linens shall be stored in non-absorbent containers or washable laundry bags until removed for laundering. Properly store soiled linens.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g REPEAT: The facility has a chlorine test kit for pools available for testing chlorine in addition to a proper chlorine kit. Cease use of the pool testing kit. Also, the facility uses quat tablets (receiving tablets today). Make sure that quat testing strips are available for testing this product. Chlorine/bleach = 100ppm Cl and Quat = 200ppm. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 There is a gap underneath the backroom door. During the inspection crickets were observed coming into the facility through the opening. Maintenance was on-site and able to repair during the inspection. Make sure that daylight is never visible around doors. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 REPEAT x2: Observed the coving to be missing from around the mopsink/back door. During the inspection the coving was replaced.  The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: There are currently no test strips available for testing the concentration of sanitizing solution. Provide test strips appropriate for the sanitizer available.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-110g Multiple items are received from the Qik N EZ kitchen with a complete and proper intact label. There are muffins and cinnamon rolls that bear no labeling. Make sure these items receive the same labeling your other products receive.  Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name; name, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g There is no QUAT test strips available for the in-use sanitizer. Provide test strips appropriate for the available sanitizers.. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b A number of wet wiping cloths were observed stored beneath the shelving on the counters. Manager indicated that staff likes to 'hide' the cloths under the shelving and then quickly grab,  wipe counters, and hide the cloths again. All the cloths were pulled from their 'hiding' places during the inspection. It is important to submerged cloths within sanitizing solution between uses in order to kill bacteria that grow on the warm, moist, and food-particle ridden cloths between uses. Provide a sanitizing solution bucket that will hold these cloths between uses. Store the buckets low and away from food storage (lower shelf within the cabinets). Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed boxes of cups and napkins stored on the floor in the back storage  room. Store single-service items at least 6" off the floor. Discussed using one of the numerous available plastic  soda pallets present in the back room. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 REPEAT: Coving to the right of the back door is missing (approximately one  foot worth). Replace the missing coving. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 There is currently no certified food handler present. Manager is new to the area. He was given information on food courses. Previous manager has been promoted to corporate. He no  longer may be considered a full time employee.  There is a Serv Safe certified employee present. Provide her information to SCDPH and make sure she submits the IDPH form for the FSSMC certificate (she should submit $35 too). Copy of IDPH form given to manager.  All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.
